stem: After an inpatient dies by suicide, several staff members and clients who knew the person are distressed. Which organizational response best reflects suicide postvention and patient-safety principles?

options.A: Avoid discussing the death with affected people unless they independently request help, because organized follow-up may intensify grief.
options.B: Focus the response on identifying which individual clinician should be blamed before offering staff or client support.
options.C: Provide immediate and ongoing support and referral resources to people affected by the suicide while the organization separately reviews contributing system factors to reduce recurrence risk.
options.D: Limit the response to completion of the client’s medical record because emotional support and event review are outside the organization’s role.

rationale: C is correct. Suicide postvention is an organized response after a suicide that supports healing, reduces harmful effects of exposure, and helps reduce suicide risk among affected people; current Suicide Prevention Resource Center guidance recommends immediate and long-term support tailored to those exposed. Separately, Joint Commission patient-safety policy expects organizations to examine root causes and contributing factors of sentinel events and make improvements to reduce recurrence risk. A is incorrect because effective postvention is proactive rather than limited to people who independently seek help. B is inconsistent with a systems-based safety response and can impede support and learning. D omits both the psychosocial needs of people exposed to the suicide and the organization’s patient-safety review responsibilities.
educational_objective: After a suicide death, support affected clients, families, and staff through organized postvention while participating in a separate systems-focused review of contributing factors to reduce future risk.
source_organization: Suicide Prevention Resource Center; The Joint Commission
source_document_title: Provide for Immediate and Long-Term Postvention; Sentinel Event FAQs and Sentinel Event Policy and Procedures
source_version_date: Current SPRC resources accessed 2026-08-17; Joint Commission Sentinel Event policy effective 2026
source_locator: SPRC, ‘What is Postvention?’ and ‘Take Action’ — organized response to facilitate healing, mitigate negative effects, reduce subsequent suicide risk, and provide immediate/long-term support. Joint Commission Sentinel Event FAQs — accredited organizations identify sentinel events, examine root causes and contributing factors, and make improvements to mitigate recurrence; Sentinel Event Policy and Procedures effective January 1, 2026
source_claim_supported: Postvention provides proactive immediate and long-term support to people exposed to a suicide; healthcare organizations also use systems-focused analysis of serious safety events to identify contributing factors and reduce recurrence rather than substituting blame for learning.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — support clients and others experiencing grief, loss, crisis, and suicide-related risk; Management of Care — participate in patient-safety and performance-improvement processes
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — suicide postvention, grief support, and systems-based safety review
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item to distinguish two related but separate responsibilities after a suicide: postvention support for people exposed to the loss and systems-focused safety review of contributing factors. The final item avoids conflating postvention itself with root-cause analysis and replaces low-value distractors with realistic organizational-response errors.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: suicide postvention / grief support / patient-safety systems review
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current SPRC postvention guidance, including 2025 provider-postvention resources, and current Joint Commission Sentinel Event policy materials. SPRC defines postvention around healing, mitigation of exposure effects, and subsequent suicide-risk reduction; Joint Commission separately supports root-cause/contributing-factor analysis and improvement.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: C deliberately uses ‘while the organization separately reviews’ so the item does not mislabel root-cause analysis as postvention. The support claim is directly supported by SPRC; the systems-review claim is directly supported by Joint Commission.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect. SPRC recommends planned, proactive immediate and long-term support rather than passive help only after affected people seek it.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect. Individual blame is not the purpose of postvention and is inconsistent with systems-focused event learning.
audit_findings.choice_C: Correct. It addresses both the psychosocial postvention needs and the separate organizational safety-review responsibility without conflating them.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect. Documentation alone is insufficient to address the needs and safety processes triggered by a suicide death.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C includes both proactive support and appropriate systems learning. None of the alternatives satisfies either complete postvention or safety-review principles.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe organizational responses after the same event and are comparable in scope; C is not correct merely because it is longer or more compassionate in tone.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is the primary category because the central nursing construct is support after suicide loss; patient-safety review provides Management of Care overlap.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited the definition of postvention, proactive versus passive support, client/staff exposure, root-cause analysis as a separate process, blame language, Joint Commission 2026 currentness, second-answer risk, and NCLEX relevance. No unresolved conflict remained.
